Machines

Seven Machines, One Mission

These machines were left on the Moon by NASA between 1967 and 1972. They helped us explore, collect data and understand the lunar surface.

Interactive

Spin the Moon

Spin the Moon with your finger or mouse! Tap a glowing circle to meet a machine.

Positions are approximate. Markers are spread apart on purpose so each one is easy to click.

About This Website

This website is created for educational purposes, sharing information about NASA’s Moon missions. All images, names and logos are the property of their respective owners.

Images & Sources

Images are credited to their original owners. NASA images and mission information are used for educational purposes; this independent project is not affiliated with NASA.

3D Moon: The Moon sphere and its surface texture are generated procedurally in this project; no external 3D Moon model was imported. The 3D scene is rendered with Three.js (r128).

Fact-check references:
NASA ALSEP Termination Report — ALSEP operations ended September 30, 1977.
Apollo 15 Mission Report — heat-flow probe deployment and drilling difficulties.
NASA: Earth in Far-Ultraviolet — Apollo 16 camera and George Carruthers.
